span: a complaint under Section 138 of the Negotiable Instruments Act, 1881 preferred by the Power of Attorney Holder is held maintainable
why: Whether a power-of-attorney holder may file the complaint; different issue from demand notice.

span: if payment is not made within the statutory period, even after issue of notice
why: Vicarious liability of directors under s.141; notice mentioned only in describing the offence.

span: in the absence of a notice of demand being served on the company and without compliance with the proviso to s.138
why: Headnote holding: without a demand notice to the company (the drawer for s.141 purposes) the complaint cannot be extended against it; demand notice treated as a necessary step.

span: The appellant thereafter issued legal notices to the respondent-accused
why: Facts of the dishonour and notices; no ruling on the need for notice.

span: The only question before the criminal court is whether the cheque issued by the accused towards the discharge of his liability was dishonoured and despite the service of demand notice, whether he had not paid the amount
why: Headnote repeating the holding that service of the demand notice and non-payment within 15 days complete the offence.

span: The appellant in that view issued notices dated 14.04.2015 through registered post

why: Records testimony that no demand notice was sent to the firm; the court's ruling on its effect is not in the passage.

span: the time period prescribed for issuance of statutory notice under Section 138 has long expired
why: Remark about why the complainant cannot start afresh; the case is about a cheque drawn on an account not maintained by the accused.
